Do NOT edit, create or delete any file under /tmp/bench/wt/ (no code edits, no tests written), do NOT run git commands that change state, and do NOT run cargo (the lead runs all builds). You MAY write throwaway Python scripts under /tmp/bench/sec1-scratch/erc1155/ for arithmetic checks and run them with `python3 -I`.

Codebase: OpenZeppelin Contracts for Stylus (Rust, Stylus SDK 0.10.10), worktree /tmp/bench/wt/sec1. It is a port of OpenZeppelin Solidity v5 contracts. Your area: contracts/src/token/erc1155/** (mod.rs, receiver.rs, utils/holder.rs, extensions/{burnable,metadata_uri,supply,uri_storage}.rs) and contracts/src/token/common/erc2981.rs. Read every non-test line in these files (tests too, when they inform expected behaviour). Compare with OpenZeppelin Solidity v5.x ERC1155, ERC1155Supply, ERC1155Burnable, ERC1155URIStorage, ERC1155Holder, ERC1155Utils, ERC2981 from your knowledge.

Stylus semantics to keep in mind:
- A `#[public]` entrypoint returning Err reverts all state changes of that call. A panic also reverts. BUT internal Rust composition does not: if library code mutates storage and then returns Err to a Rust caller that handles the Err and continues, the partial writes persist. Flag library code paths that catch an Err from a mutating function and continue.
- External calls: `Call::new_mutating(self)` / `Call::new()` / `call::static_call`. Return data must be validated (code existence, selector, length). TestVM: a call to an address without a mock "succeeds" and returns the last mocked data; addresses have no code unless `vm.set_code` is used.
- Reentrancy is off by default in Stylus (feature `reentrant` enables it).
- The library does not have Solidity inheritance: extensions are separate storage structs (or wrap the base), so check whether extension state can desynchronise from the base (e.g., Supply's total_supply / total_supply_all vs balances).
- ruint/alloy U256 operators: check whether `+`, `*`, `-` panic or wrap in this build (look at how the code uses checked_*, saturating, wrapping, or the crate's `math::storage` helpers `add_assign_checked` / `add_assign_unchecked` in contracts/src/utils/math/storage). Release profile has debug-assertions = false.

Your task:
1. Write down the invariants each contract in your area must keep (e.g. for each id: sum of balances == total_supply(id); total_supply_all == sum over ids; only owner or approved operator can move tokens; batch ids/values lengths must match; acceptance checks call onERC1155Received/onERC1155BatchReceived on contracts and check the selector; set_approval_for_all rejects operator zero; burn requires authorization; URI semantics; ERC-2981: royalty fraction <= denominator, receiver != 0, royalty_info computation sale_price * fraction / denominator with correct overflow behaviour, token royalty overrides default, reset semantics; ERC-165 IDs correct).
2. Attack each invariant by reading the state-changing code paths: missing checks, wrong order of effects/interactions, off-by-one, integer overflow/underflow, wrong error, access-control gaps, mismatches with Solidity semantics, unchecked receiver return data, events emitted with wrong args (TransferSingle vs TransferBatch rules for single-element batches), duplicate ids in batches.
3. For every suspected bug, give: file:line, what breaks, a concrete trigger scenario (step by step), the impact, a severity estimate (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Informational) with justification, your confidence, and a sketch of a unit test (TestVM-based; harness facts: `TestVM::default()`, `T::from(&vm)`, `vm.set_sender`, `vm.set_code(addr, code)`, `vm.mock_call(addr, calldata, Ok(ret)/Err(revert_data))`, `vm.get_emitted_logs()`; fixtures ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE in contracts/src/test_utils.rs) that would FAIL on the current code and pass after a fix, plus the suggested fix.
4. List every #[ignore]d test in your area and classify it (real bug / wrong test / harness limitation) with evidence.

Be rigorous: verify each claim against the actual code (quote the lines) and do not report speculative issues as bugs; put uncertain ones in a separate "needs verification" list. Report invariants that HOLD briefly with the reason. Final answer: a structured report (invariants with held/broken, suspected bugs with the fields above, needs-verification list, ignored tests). No length limit, but be precise.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

209	impl Erc1155Supply {
210	    /// Extended version of [`Erc1155::_update`] that updates the supply of
211	    /// tokens.
212	    ///
213	    /// NOTE: The ERC-1155 acceptance check is not performed in this function.
214	    /// See [`Self::_update_with_acceptance_check`] instead.
215	    ///
216	    /// # Arguments
217	    ///
218	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
219	    /// * `from` - Account of the sender.
220	    /// * `to` - Account of the recipient.
221	    /// * `token_ids` - Array of all token id.
222	    /// * `values` - Array of all amount of tokens to be supplied.
223	    ///
224	    /// # Errors
225	    ///
226	    /// * [`erc1155::Error::InvalidArrayLength`] - If length of `ids` is not
227	    ///   equal to length of `values`.
228	    /// * [`erc1155::Error::InsufficientBalance`] - If `value` is greater than
229	    ///   the balance of the `from` account.
230	    ///
231	    /// # Events
232	    ///
233	    /// * [`erc1155::TransferSingle`] - If the arrays contain one element.
234	    /// * [`erc1155::TransferBatch`] - If the arrays contain more than one
235	    ///   element.
236	    ///
237	    /// # Panics
238	    ///
239	    /// * If updated balance and/or supply exceeds [`U256::MAX`], may happen
240	    ///   during the `mint` operation.
241	    fn _update(
242	        &mut self,
243	        from: Address,
244	        to: Address,
245	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
246	        values: Vec<U256>,
247	    ) -> Result<(), erc1155::Error> {
248	        self.erc1155._update(from, to, token_ids.clone(), values.clone())?;
249	
250	        if from.is_zero() {
251	            for (&token_id, &value) in token_ids.iter().zip(values.iter()) {
252	                self.total_supply.setter(token_id).add_assign_checked(
253	                    value,
254	                    "should not exceed `U256::MAX` for `total_supply`",
255	                );
256	            }
257	
258	            let total_mint_value = values.iter().sum();
259	            self.total_supply_all.add_assign_checked(
260	                total_mint_value,
261	                "should not exceed `U256::MAX` for `total_supply_all`",
262	            );
263	        }
264	
265	        if to.is_zero() {
266	            for (token_id, &value) in token_ids.into_iter().zip(values.iter()) {
267	                /*
268	                 * SAFETY: Overflow not possible:
269	                 * values[i] <= balance_of(from, token_ids[i]) <=
270	                 * total_supply(token_ids[i])
271	                 */
272	                self.total_supply.setter(token_id).sub_assign_unchecked(value);
273	            }
274	
275	            let total_burn_value: U256 = values.into_iter().sum();
276	            /*
277	             * SAFETY: Overflow not possible:
278	             * total_burn_value = sum_i(values[i]) <=
279	             * sum_i(total_supply(ids[i])) <= total_supply_all
280	             */
281	            self.total_supply_all.sub_assign_unchecked(total_burn_value);
282	        }
283	        Ok(())
284	    }

289	        to: Address,

291	        values: Vec<U256>,
292	        data: &Bytes,
293	    ) -> Result<(), erc1155::Error> {
294	        self._update(from, to, ids.clone(), values.clone())?;
295	
296	        if !to.is_zero() {
297	            self.erc1155._check_on_erc1155_received(
298	                self.vm().msg_sender(),
299	                from,
300	                to,
301	                erc1155::Erc1155ReceiverData::new(ids, values),
302	                data.to_vec().into(),
303	            )?;
304	        }
305	
306	        Ok(())

317	            return Err(erc1155::Error::InvalidReceiver(
318	                erc1155::ERC1155InvalidReceiver { receiver: to },

320	        }

322	            Address::ZERO,
323	            to,
324	            ids,
325	            values,
326	            data,
327	        )?;

329	    }
